faqs.a:
(a)
Before a permit is issued pursuant to this article, the applicant shall pay to the
               city a permit fee, which shall be determined annually in accordance with a fee schedule
               adopted by the city council by resolution. Fees will be reasonably related to the
               costs inherent in managing the public rights-of-way. As used in this article, these
               costs include, but are not necessarily limited to, the costs of permitting rights-of-way
               occupants, verifying rights-of-way occupation, mapping rights-of-way occupations,
               review and approval of a traffic control plan, inspecting job sites and rights-of-way
               restorations, administering this article, and costs incurred by the city relating
               to the degradation of the rights-of-way, (i.e., the cost to achieve a level of restoration
               as determined by the city at the time the permit is issued).
(b)
Recognizing that excavation or disturbance of the right-of-way results in degradation
               of such right-of-way that may be difficult to restore to its original condition, a
               portion of the permit fee relates to degradation/restoration costs. The portion of
               the permit fee relating to degradation/restoration costs shall be as established by
               annual resolution and equally apportioned by the city in cases where the applicant
               demonstrates to the satisfaction of the director that the excavation proposed will
               be used by two or more entities, legally and financially unrelated, for the installation,
               maintenance, or repair of facilities.
(c)
Any permit for temporary use or occupation of the public rights-of-way, where there
               is no construction involved, shall not require payment of a degradation fee as part
               of the permit fee.
(d)
Any contractor who excavates or otherwise disturbs a right-of-way shall, following
               such excavation, construction, or disturbance, restore the right-of-way according
               to the following criteria:
(1)
Any trench or hole cut into a street will significantly decrease the remaining life
               of the street. The impact on the degradation of the street can be similar, regardless
               of street age or condition. Subject to subsection (b) of this section, all fees will
               be applied equally to all streets regardless of age or condition.
(2)
Degradation fees shall be based on the actual cost of the work required to prevent
               further damage to the street, and such fees shall be reevaluated annually.
(e)
That portion of any permit fee relating to degradation/restoration costs shall be
               segregated by the city into an account to cover general street maintenance and construction.
(Code 1981, § 27-205; Ord. No. 3717, § 1, 8-27-2001)
